title: the DSG Deepearth areas 20-21
audit_comment: The DSG Deepearth areas 20-21 pin Area 20 (the Lava Caves with their balcony over the lava sea, the fire giant outpost, the island lairs, the granite lava boats and the king's island castle) and Area 21 (the Elemental Vortex of Fire with its 100-ft hole, the Wisdom-Check stare, the 8d8 passage and the molten whirlpool).

banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 20-21, R543: printed pp. 91-92 (pdf 92-93) - the individual area key crosses the fire: Area 20 the Lava Caves (the balcony cavern overlooking the vast amphitheatre of molten rock, its weekly eruptions, the cataclysm-split cave half fallen away and baked brittle; the 400-foot climbable cliff, the crags and columns, the 1,000-foot ceiling losing chunks daily, the ocean-like swells and splashing; the fire giant outpost of about 20 with its dozen hell hounds and always-mounted tunnel guard; the rock-island lairs of fire giants and lava children at 50% per island; the porpoise-like magmen, the dwelling fire bats, the savage magma para-elementals; the once-a-decade elemental invasions repelled by the joined giants and lava children; the granite lava boats 80-240 feet long at 20% width, twin-masted over 160 feet, an oar pair per 40 feet; and the fire giant king's island castle with its 120-foot flank-towered harbor), and Area 21 the Elemental Vortex of Fire (the waterless, wind-sucked region where a torch dies 50% of the time; the 1,000-by-300-foot cavern with its rotted formations; the perfectly circular 100-foot hole ringed in flame, hypnotic and bottomless, a Wisdom Check after one round of staring compelling the failed jump; the vortex gate to the Plane of Fire; the 1d6 fire elementals guarding it and the 50% chance of 1d6 efreeti, salamanders, azer, fire bats or elemental grue reinforcing on the first and every other round; the hot dry sulphurous air; the 8d8-per-round passage falling as if feather-fallen, escapable by levitation or fly within five rounds, committed after, ten rounds to the volcanic landscape; and the two Prime connections - 50% Area 21, 50% the lava sea whirlpool that draws boats within 500 feet).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~11688-11932) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (capture idx 210 = the printed pp. 91-92 window, with the p. 92 tail and the Area 22 head carried in idx 212); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the weekly eruptions, the 400-ft cliff, the 1,000-ft ceiling, the 20-giant outpost with its dozen hounds, the 50% island races, the decade invasions, the 80/240-ft boats at 20% width with the 160-ft mast threshold and 40-ft oar spacing, the 120-ft harbor mouth with its dozen-per-tower, the 50% torch, the 1,000x300-ft cavern, the 100-ft hole, the one-round stare, the 1d6 elementals, the 50% 1d6 reinforcements, the 8d8 passage, the five- and ten-round windows, the 50/50 connections and the 500-ft whirlpool draw; the only garbles settled cross-read (the djvu 848 and 5096 for the capture 8d8 and 50%, the capture ld6 and ajarge for the djvu 1d6 and a large). SEAMS: the R518 water-travel analog (the lava boats), the Monster Manual denizens (the fire giants, hell hounds, efreeti, salamanders, azer, elemental grue, lava children), the PHB feather fall/levitation/fly and the Wisdom Check, and the Plane of Fire lore. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533-R542 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the eruption week, the cliff and ceiling feet, the outpost giants and hounds and guard minimum, the island race percentage, the invasion decades, the boat length bounds and width percentage and mast threshold and oar spacing, the harbor mouth and tower garrison, the torch percentage, the cavern diameter and height, the hole diameter, the stare rounds, the reinforcement percentage, the escape and passage rounds, the emergence percentage and the whirlpool draw feet, with the 1d6, 8d8 and 1d6 dice pinned as count-sides const pairs. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas. The water-travel/MM/PHB seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnalEruptWeekDays
consts.comment: the eruptions of smoke, fire and poison gas here are much less common than in Area 19 - perhaps one eruption per week.

consts.name: dnalCliffFt
consts.comment: the cave floor drops off to the northeast in a 400-foot cliff, with enough cracks and ledges to make climbing possible.

consts.name: dnalCeilMinFt
consts.comment: in most cases the stony ceiling is at least 1,000 feet above the surface of the lava sea.

consts.name: dnalOutpostGiants
consts.comment: the fire giant outpost usually holds about 20 individuals.

consts.name: dnalOutpostHounds
consts.comment: the outpost giants are accompanied by a dozen hell hounds.

consts.name: dnalGuardMin
consts.comment: at least one giant and one hell hound guard the access tunnel at all times.

consts.name: dnalIslandRacePct
consts.comment: a given island lair has a 50% chance of either race, fire giants or lava children.

consts.name: dnalInvasionDecades
consts.comment: the elemental invasions occur about once every decade.

consts.name: dnalBoatLenLoFt
consts.comment: the lava boats range in length from 80 feet (the low bound).

consts.name: dnalBoatLenHiFt
consts.comment: the lava boats range in length up to 240 feet (the high bound).

consts.name: dnalBoatWidthPct
consts.comment: a lava boat has a width of about 20% of its length.

consts.name: dnalMastThresholdFt
consts.comment: boats longer than 160 feet are equipped with a pair of masts, while the shorter boats have only single masts.

consts.name: dnalOarsPerFt
consts.comment: each boat has one pair of oars for every 40 feet of length.

consts.name: dnalHarborMouthFt
consts.comment: the harbor entrance is only 120 feet wide.

consts.name: dnalTowerGiants
consts.comment: the harbor entrance is protected on each flank by a high tower manned by a dozen fire giants with a large supply of boulders to hurl at unwelcome intruders.

consts.name: dnalTorchOutPct
consts.comment: the entrance-tunnel wind is 50% likely to extinguish a torch.

consts.name: dnalCavernDiaFt
consts.comment: the tunnel ends in a huge cavern 1,000 feet in diameter.

consts.name: dnalCavernHtFt
consts.comment: the vortex cavern is 300 feet high.

consts.name: dnalHoleDiaFt
consts.comment: at the center a perfectly circular hole 100 feet across drops to the unknown depths below, red and orange fingers of flame flickering around its circumference and occasionally flaring as high as the ceiling.

consts.name: dnalStareRounds
consts.comment: any character staring down the hypnotically swirling hole for more than a single round must make a Wisdom Check.

consts.name: dnalElementalDice
consts.comment: the fingers of fire around the vortex contain 1d6 fire elementals (the die count).

consts.name: dnalElementalSides
consts.comment: the vortex holds 1d6 fire elementals (the die sides).

consts.name: dnalReinforcePct
consts.comment: there is an additional 50% chance that reinforcements immediately emerge from the vortex to battle invaders.

consts.name: dnalReinforceDice
consts.comment: the vortex reinforcements number 1d6 (the die count).

consts.name: dnalReinforceSides
consts.comment: the vortex reinforcements number 1d6 (the die sides).

consts.name: dnalVortexDmgDice
consts.comment: any creatures entering the vortex who are not completely immune to fire suffer 8d8 of damage per round (the die count).

consts.name: dnalVortexDmgSides
consts.comment: the vortex passage deals 8d8 damage per round to non-immune creatures (the die sides).

consts.name: dnalReverseRounds
consts.comment: the levitation or fly escape window is five rounds after entering the vortex.

consts.name: dnalPassageRounds
consts.comment: the entire vortex passage requires 10 rounds.

consts.name: dnalEmergePct
consts.comment: anyone re-entering the vortex has a 50% chance of emerging in Area 21.

consts.name: dnalWhirlpoolDrawFt
consts.comment: any lava boats venturing within 500 feet of the molten whirlpool are drawn in as if in water.

bools.name: dnalBalconyCave
bools.comment: the lava caves shown on the map are a small portion of a huge underground expanse running many miles north and east; the displayed cavern is situated like a balcony overlooking a vast amphitheatre of fire and molten rock.

bools.name: dnalTunnelSameRisk
bools.comment: the tunnel leading to this area is very hot with the same damage potential as the tunnel to Area 19, and characters in Area 20 stand about the same chance of sustaining damage as in Area 19.

bools.name: dnalHalfFallen
bools.comment: the cavern is a portion of a natural cave split by cataclysmic geological forces: fully half of the original cave has fallen away to the encroaching lava, and the remainder is baked brittle with a layer of smoky residue on all surfaces.

bools.name: dnalSeaPanorama
bools.comment: the cliff drops away to a sea of lava lit by a dull red hellish glow; crags jut like forlorn islands, far tunnels branch off, and stone columns rise to the ceiling supporting the massive weight above.

bools.name: dnalDailyChunks
bools.comment: every day a few chunks of stone and earth break free and tumble into the inferno below, and ceiling fissures vent heat and smoke toward the surface mountain range.

bools.name: dnalSeaSwells
bools.comment: the lava surface is tossed by a series of swells like an ocean surface, caused by internal convulsions far beneath; the lava splashes against the containing cliffs like an angry sea at its shore.

bools.name: dnalOutpostControl
bools.comment: the balcony cavern is guarded by a large outpost of fire giants, one of the few avenues to the fiery lands; the denizens carefully control who travels here, and the entire force repels any intruders discovered.

bools.name: dnalIslandLairs
bools.comment: rock islands scattered among the liquid rock serve as lairs for additional bands of fire giants and groups of lava children - each island holds only one type, the two races preferring separate lairs though they do not usually fight.

bools.name: dnalMagmenSea
bools.comment: great numbers of magmen live in the lava sea, splashing through the molten rock like porpoises; a few occasionally climb to the balcony cave to dive back down, an activity the fire giants view with amused tolerance.

bools.name: dnalFireBatsDwell
bools.comment: many fire bats dwell in the vast cavern, clinging to the lofty ceiling or soaring through the scorching air as they travel across Deepearth.

bools.name: dnalMagmaPara
bools.comment: para-elementals of magma dwell within the molten rock - less common than the magmen but far more dangerous, forming in the hottest areas and reaching upward to attack anyone within reach; even the fire giants in their lava boats are not immune.

bools.name: dnalConquerorForays
bools.comment: the Area 21 elemental vortex is the source of would-be conquerors: fire elementals, efreeti, salamanders and lower-plane allies foray into the sea to wage war, and the lava children and fire giants join forces against the common enemy - spectacular battles of lava boat fleets, flying boulders and thousands of creatures; the denizens have always driven off the invaders, each foray made with more force than the one before.

bools.name: dnalHeatOnly
bools.comment: the only real resource of the area is heat, which is difficult to transport to where it might be needed.

bools.name: dnalBoats
bools.comment: the fire giants have sculpted massive granite boats they row or sail across the fiery liquid - wide stone paddles like galley oars, sails of a mysterious heat-resistant perhaps magically treated cloth hoisted when gusts sweep the sea, and a stone tiller in the stern; a forceful gust pushes the clumsy Viking-longship-like boats along at surface-sailing clip.

bools.name: dnalKingIsland
bools.comment: on a large island several miles from the balcony cave resides the fire giant king: the entire island tunneled and carved into a massive castle with tall towers and a high wall meeting the lava on all sides but one, where a breach opens into a lava-filled harbor with stone docks.

bools.name: dnalNoWater
bools.comment: water is nonexistent in this region; when it leaks into the area it turns instantly to steam.

bools.name: dnalWindForce
bools.comment: the air is usually breathable, and fresh air is sucked in through the entrance tunnel with a force capable of blowing out candles and unsheltered lanterns.

bools.name: dnalVortexRegion
bools.comment: the region is reached by crossing the lava sea or through the tunnel from Area 18; it is uncomfortably hot, and characters approaching through the tunnel run the same damage risks as in the other linking passages of the area.

bools.name: dnalRottedFormations
bools.comment: the cavern formed naturally, but tremendous heat has long since dried and rotted its once-fabulous cave formations; the heat here has the same effect on characters as in Areas 19 and 20.

bools.name: dnalFlatFloor
bools.comment: the cavern floor is smooth and flat except at the very center.

bools.name: dnalHypnoticJump
bools.comment: if the Wisdom Check fails, the character is compelled to jump into the hole and journey to the Plane of Fire.

bools.name: dnalNoOtherExits
bools.comment: the cavern has no entrances or exits other than the tunnel from Area 18 and the hole in the floor.

bools.name: dnalVortexGate
bools.comment: the hole is not a pit to the lava sea that flows beneath: through tremendous heat, pressure and arcane force it has become a vortex to the Plane of Fire, through which creatures of that fiery region journey to the Prime Material Plane without being summoned, and properly protected Prime Plane creatures journey to the Plane of Fire.

bools.name: dnalElementalGuard
bools.comment: the only denizens are those journeyed from the Plane of Fire, fortunately not ranging far; the flickering fingers of fire contain fire elementals of randomly determined size, which remain in or very near the vortex and combine forces to prevent Prime Plane creatures from entering it.

bools.name: dnalReinforceRoster
bools.comment: the reinforcements are efreeti, salamanders, azer, fire bats and elemental grue.

bools.name: dnalReinforceCadence
bools.comment: reinforcements are checked on the first round contact is made and every other round thereafter - the third, fifth, seventh, etc.

bools.name: dnalSulphurAir
bools.comment: there is a minimum amount of breathable air in the chamber, and that is hot, dry and sulphurous; little else of value can be found here.

bools.name: dnalFeatherFall
bools.comment: the vortex is an extraplanar location not subject to normal gravity: anything entering it descends as if under a feather fall spell.

bools.name: dnalFlyReverse
bools.comment: magic such as levitation or fly spells allows a character to reverse course and emerge from the vortex if cast within five rounds of entering.

bools.name: dnalCommitted
bools.comment: after the escape window the character is committed to a journey to the Plane of Fire.

bools.name: dnalPlaneArrival
bools.comment: after the passage the character stands on a bleak volcanic landscape of eruptions, geysers and flowing lava, the vortex evident directly behind as a chute into the depths of a large volcano.

bools.name: dnalTwoConnections
bools.comment: the vortex has two connections to the Prime Plane in roughly the same area - re-entering grants a 50% chance of emerging in Area 21 and a 50% chance in the lava sea; the lower vortex appears as a giant whirlpool of molten rock directly below the Area 21 one, and is the source of the elemental armies that attack the fire giants and lava children.

examples.note: the lava caves: weekly eruptions, the 400-ft cliff, the 1,000-ft ceiling.
the outpost: 20 giants, a dozen hounds, at least one of each guarding at all times.
the islands: 50% per race, the once-a-decade invasions.
